property_method.plan: NRTL (activity model, ideal-gas vapour) in every block; Wilson as a variant
property_method.paper: HYSYS 'glycol package' (Table 1, p.3); its model and parameters are not printed
property_method.reason: Water, ethylene oxide (EO), MEG and DEG are polar, associating liquids with no light gas, which CHEPTA's method guide (v0.6.2) puts in an activity model (NRTL or UNIQUAC). The plant spans 10-3534 kPa: the feed train, reactor and pumps (3450-3534 kPa) hold liquid only, but EVA_1 makes vapour at 1600 kPa and 202.8 C with an ideal-gas vapour, and EVA_1, the reactor (199 C) and streams 3 and 15 (200 and 199.2 C) are above EO's critical temperature (468.92 K = 195.77 C in chepta 0.6.2 components.json), where the method guide (rule 1) says an activity model needs every liquid component below its critical temperature. Pairs in chepta 0.6.2 binaries.json: water + MEG NRTL fitted (Kamihama 2012, 101.3 kPa); DEG + MEG NRTL fitted (Yang 2014, 40 kPa bubble temperatures); DEG + water NRTL from the ChemSep databank; EO + water only Wilson (ChemSep databank); EO + MEG and EO + DEG none. Under NRTL every EO pair is therefore estimated from Modified UNIFAC 2.0 (with CHEPTA's warning); under Wilson, EO + water comes from the databank and the EO + glycol pairs are still estimated. NRTL is kept as the main method because it carries the fitted glycol pairs; Wilson is run as a variant (one liquid; no liquid split is expected, Lab's expectation). CPA, used for glycol + water by Othman 2024, is not in CHEPTA 0.6.2 (roadmap M3). What CHEPTA does with EO above its critical temperature is the first step of the run plan.
